ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A long wooden plank is moving to the right with a constant velocity $v_{0}$ on a smooth horizontal surface. A small slider is gently placed on the rightmost end of the plank with no initial velocity. The masses of the slider and the plank are $m$ and $2m$, respectively, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between them is $\mu$. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$.

1. Determine the magnitude of their common velocity when the slider is stationary relative to the plank.
2. At a certain moment, the velocity of the plank is twice the velocity of the slider. Determine the distance from the slider to the rightmost end of the plank at this moment.
3. If a horizontal external force to the right is applied to the plank at the same time as the slider is gently placed on the rightmost end of the plank, such that the plank maintains uniform linear motion until the slider comes to rest relative to the plank, determine the time of motion of the slider during this process.
4. If a horizontal external force to the right is applied to the plank at the same time as the slider is gently placed on the rightmost end of the plank, such that the plank maintains uniform linear motion until the slider comes to rest relative to the plank, calculate the work done by the external force during this process.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a long wooden plank is placed on a smooth horizontal surface; the plank as a whole moves to the right along the horizontal direction, and on the right side there is a rightward velocity arrow labeled v0; a small slider is located above the right end of the plank. Take the rightward direction as the positive direction. Reasoning: 1. When there is no external force, the slider is subjected to a rightward kinetic friction force μmg, so a_slider = μg; the plank is subjected to a leftward friction force μmg, and the mass of the plank is 2m, so a_plank = -μg/2. Thus v_slider = μgt, v_plank = v0 - μgt/2. When the two are relatively at rest, their velocities are equal: μgt = v0 - μgt/2, giving t = 2v0/(3μg), and the common velocity v_all = μg·2v0/(3μg) = 2v0/3. 2. When the velocity of the plank is twice the velocity of the slider, v0 - μgt/2 = 2μgt, giving t = 2v0/(5μg). At this time the displacement of the right end of the plank is s_plank = v0t - (μg)t^2/4, and the displacement of the slider is s_slider = (μg)t^2/2. The distance from the slider to the right end of the plank is x = s_plank - s_slider = v0t - 3(μg)t^2/4. Substituting t = 2v0/(5μg), gives x = 7v0^2/(25μg). 3. If an external force makes the plank maintain uniform linear motion, then the velocity of the plank is always v0. The slider is still accelerated to the right by kinetic friction, a = μg, until the slider's velocity reaches v0, so t = v0/(μg). 4. For the plank to maintain uniform velocity, the external force needs to counteract the leftward friction force exerted by the slider on the plank, therefore F = μmg. During this process the displacement of the plank is v0t = v0·v0/(μg), and the work done by the external force is W = F·v0t = μmg·v0^2/(μg) = mv0^2.
